tabs.label: Sections
describe.shellBle: Radios in range, found by the shell.
describe.windowsBle: Radios in range, found by Windows.
describe.tcp: A radio on the network, by its address. Companion firmware built with Wi-Fi listens on port 5000.
describe.demo: A pretend radio, for a look around without hardware.
port.board: A port on the computer's board
step.hello: Waiting for the radio to answer
hint.ble: Is the radio on and close by? It must not be connected to another phone or computer.
hint.serial: Does the cable carry data, not just charge? Is the port free of other programs?
hint.tcp: Check the address, and that the radio is on the same network.
list.empty: Looking… Turn the radio on and keep it close.
list.noPorts: No radio on USB. Plug one in with a cable.
list.morePorts: Ports that do not look like a radio
tips.ble: The radio is on, close by, and not connected to another phone or computer: a radio connected elsewhere stops showing itself.
tips.serial: The cable carries data, not only charge, and no other program holds the port. A radio shows up here a few seconds after it is plugged in.
pair.cardTitle: The radio asks for a PIN
pair.cardLabel: The PIN on the radio's screen; 123456 unless it was changed
pair.cardLabelPhone: Any digits: the phone asks on its own screen
address.label: The radio's address
signal.quietWhy: It is off, too far away, or connected to another phone.
noLink.title: This browser cannot reach a radio: it has neither Web Bluetooth nor Web Serial.
noLink.browser: Chrome or Edge can. Or use the desktop or phone application, which carry their own Bluetooth and USB.
noLink.shell: The shell offered no link; this is a bug.
pair.title: Pair
pair.label: PIN on the radio's screen, or any digits for a phone
badge.attention: A node of yours needs a look
empty.pickChat: Pick a conversation, or start one with +.
error.pickRadio: pick a radio from the list
error.pickPort: pick a port from the list
error.noGatt: this device has no GATT server
error.notPaired: {name} is not paired with this computer, or no longer trusts the pairing.
error.phonePairing: {name} was not paired: the PIN was not entered, or was not the radio's (123456 unless changed).
error.bleWantsPairing: {error}. The radio wants a paired link: pair it in Windows Settings → Bluetooth with its PIN (123456 unless changed), or remove and pair again if it was re-flashed.
serial.speedBoot: 1200 tells nRF52 and RP2040 boards to restart into their bootloader.
serial.speedBad: A port takes a whole number from 300 to 4000000.
serial.hint.auto: By the board: DTR for a board with its own USB, nothing for one behind a bridge.
serial.hint.off-off: ESP32 behind a bridge: Heltec V3, T-Beam, LilyGo T3
serial.hint.off-on: Holds an ESP32 in reset, so the radio stays silent. No MeshCore board needs it.
serial.hint.on-off: nRF52: T-Echo, RAK4631, T114 · ESP32 with its own USB: Xiao C6, S3
serial.hint.on-on: If the board wants both. The app lowers them before it closes the port.
journal.status.open: the log holds the port · the radio is not connected
journal.outcome.text: The radio answers in words, not frames
journal.outcome.loader: The board is in flashing mode
journal.outcome.loaderLine: The ESP32 waits for firmware and answers nothing else.
journal.outcome.garbageLine: The board sends bytes, but they never make a frame.
journal.outcome.silentLine: The cable only charges, the radio is off, or its firmware does not talk over USB.
journal.textPlaceholder: Text to the port, e.g. mode usb
journal.rule.end: Check over · {seconds} s · port closed, lines lowered
journal.entry.frame: A frame from the radio, code {code}
journal.entry.restart: restarting the radio: RTS on for 0.2 s
journal.empty: What goes along the cable shows here.
passwordKept.phone: Kept in the phone's secure storage.
